item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.description: Maybe it's egotism, maybe it's real, maybe it's maybelline.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The SCP refers to a hypothetical anomaly. A new "Foundation," which operates extraordinarily similarly to ours, almost the exact same but for a few differences, which has been clearly operating for years upon years, has suddenly come to our knowledge. Surely, the only way they've been existing for so long without us knowing is if they were using an anomaly to hide themselves… right? Surely, no one matches the Foundation in their ability to hide themselves from the rest of the world…

Right?

Central Narrative: The narrative is going to follow the first encounter between our SCP Foundation, and the PCS Foundation (Process, Condemn, Shield), and then followed up by a MTF exploration of a PCS facility in hunting for the SCP, then recounting an exact replica of the events that occurred at the PCS facility, except it's an interview recounting the exact same events occurring at a SCP facility. By the end, no actual SCP is recovered, or even hinted at existing, hopefully leaving the reader asking if it's possible that just maybe two foundations were so good at hiding that up until now, they hid from each other.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I know theoretical/non-existent SCPs have been done before, but I'm hoping the description here is enough of a hook to keep things going.

Additional Notes: I know I'm not the greatest at summarizations. It may need some.. work. I'd be happy to clarify anything if the need should be there. Additionally, I sort of jumped the gun and wrote up an unfinished draft. If anyone would like, I'd be happy to let you read it, although it needs some heavy revising.

item.title: "Intro to Thaumaturgy" College Textbook
item.description: A pre-owned magic textbook
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Page Layout: An initial standard page going over the published editions of the book, and a log of incomplete and poorly copied extracts of the text without magic supposedly due to low quality. Followed by an up-to-date article documenting a edited copy of the tome, with a log of the different corrections made by a disenfranchised undergraduate of the establishment that require the book. Containment procedures allow for the book to be borrowed by approved request.

Elevator Pitch: A secondhand university thaumaturgy textbook which is defunct and a scam, corrected by a angry ex-student (of the institution using it as required reading) to make it functional.

+ Show whatever
- Hide whatever

Central Narrative: The book is drawn to the foundation's attention when it is incredulously found via web-crawlers on online book. It is quickly scrubbed from the website due to Foundation concerns about secrecy. A team of researchers are tasked with tracking down copies of the book but all that can be found are monochrome, poorly reproduced photocopies which are useless assisting thaumaturgical practices.

They receive a package from a disgruntled student of a only to discover it is a textbook for a specific professor who charges $25,000 USD (or relative small fortune) or "a year's servitude to dark forces" for it. The book is covered in angry notes expressing frustration in the inaccuracies of it such as " What am I supposed to use?? Pig's blood or wolf?" and "There's no godsdamn way that is an acceptable salt circle", as well as several corrections in order to make the rituals and magic work as intended. The Foundation reclassifies the published versions as non-anomalous and classifies the only anomalous version to be the corrected one.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The thaumaturgy methods and descriptions in an academic way and the premise that not even magic prevents you from being screwed over by the educational system.

Additional Notes: Would appreciate idea on how the actual corrected book is anomalous and not just containing data that can be used to create anomalies, and any areas of thaumaturgy on the SCP universe I should try and include in the photocopy example extracts?

item.title: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.description: My third attempt at SCPs again. Need critique and if worthy greenlight.
item.content:encoded:
Idea Post:

Seeking Greenlights: Primarily Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror a lot, Drama/Emotional a good deal, History a little.

Page Layout (Optional): Basic special containment procedures and description followed by how it was obtained, then testing logs, and finally incident reports (maybe).

Elevator Pitch: Photobook slash journal used by a former researcher working at an asylum (the early ’50s to ’70s) studying primarily murderous and violent patients. People who place a photo in the book begin to have their memories and their personalities overwritten with psychotic patients.

Central Narrative: I want to highlight the malpractices and the sickening practices of asylums that studied the brains of ‘psychotic’ individuals. Reports of weird experiments have always been rumored and very few reports survive from these places because some of these acts were perpetrated by leading scientists who used this research to better our understanding of psychology. There are even reports of human sacrifices and brutal use of pagan rituals and some real dark sh. Whether or not these are real stories says what if they were really basically.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is unique in my opinion are the stories the imprinted patients can tell to people, the horrors they experienced, and how it happened.

Additional Notes: I know there are no factual claims to the horrors of such asylums in real life but I just want to tell the story, please don’t come to tell me why it isn't factual. It's SCP it ain’t meant to be factual it's meant to be fun!

Central Narrative: the house generates people who share physical experiences, and immediately causes one of them to be placed into a situation where they will die. That status is revoked when the second person sent through, a higher level operator specializing in Keter Class wet work, becomes the 'sole survivor.' Rather than experiencing a coming together of support and love of his other copies after grieving together, creating a unit far more capable than most, the Sole Survivor experiences their death three times and has a mental breakdown, joining the Chaos.

item.title: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.description: A simple 25¢ coin that can multiply
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-#### “The Infinite Quarter” is a 2019 San Antonio Mission Texas Quarter with the head side scratched out with a unknown instrument. The quarter seems like an average coin but when left unobserved the coin will start to rapidly multiply until observed or all open space is occupied. All other instances of the scp do not share the same anomalous duplication ability as the main coin and will only share the ability of ceasing duplication when the coins are observed though if one were to observe a duplicated instance of the coin and not the original coin it will not stop the original from duplicating.

Central Narrative: The coin would of first been discovered when foundation agents caught wind of a man who seemed to of out of the blue came into a fortune oddly enough in quarters. Upon investigating and obvious administration of amnestic, they discovered a shoe box completely full of quarters. It wasn’t until the agent investigating the box looked away and then back to discover that the box had begun to overflow with quarters before stopping. After finding the anomalous coin they brought it to the foundation and contain it in a specially made plastic case big enough to fit a single quarter.

** Hook/Attention-Grabber:** All duplicated instances of the coin will be in perfect condition and not sharing any of the scratch marks on the head side of the coin like the original does. I had also thought to make it so that the actual original coin is always the easiest to spot as to make it more easier to be observed to warrant its duplication stopping when viewed.

** Additional notes:** possible idea is the scp foundation will sometimes use this scp for possible funding for resources and the like.

item.title: The Jukebug
item.description: What if that song you got stuck in your head stayed there?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror
Page Format: I plan to use the standard page format, adding in interviews and audio logs to tell the stories of three separate cases.

Elevator Pitch: An auditory cognitohazard that latches onto the brain waves of a person until the afflicted person hears a “catchy" song. Once the afflicted has a song stuck in their head, the anomaly perverts the lyrics to encourage the afflicted to act out intrusive thoughts. The anomaly can lie dormant for up to three days without a song to embed itself into, before eventually dissipating. The anomaly can be detected through basic brain activity scans, appearing in the shape of an insect on images of the brain. If a song is introduced that the afflicted finds catchy, the anomaly will stay undetected by the afflicted for two more days. During which it will play the song excessively in their mind. Anytime the afflicted sings the song, their brainwaves are modified to transmit the anomaly into the minds of others, starting a separate cycle. After the two day infection period, the anomaly begins to goad the original afflicted. The more the afflicted resists, the harder it pushes with symptoms ranging in severity. The Foundation can eradicate the anomalous brain activity by playing music that lacks (in the opinion of the listener) pleasant rhythm or rhyme, for 18 hours.

It is unclear if this anomaly is merely a phenomenon or an entity. No evidence of an entity occupying the physical body of any afflicted people exist, other than vivid descriptions of a singing insect-like creature seen during the REM cycles of the afflicted, in the first several days of exposure. The vivid and consistent descriptions of this creature, coupled with the insect-shaped brain image, have lead to a dichotomy in the observing staff. Those who believe it is merely a phenomenon, which the evidence seems to support the most, have developed the current SCP protocols. A separate team, continues to search for evidence of what they call the “Jukebug.”
Central Narrative: Multiple accounts of different instances of the “Jukebug,” including: the aftermath of a child's birthday party, a surgeon, and a musician working on their newest song.

Hook: I think the idea that you could have been infected by this SCP and it’s already too late is spine-chilling and compelling enough to draw people in.

Additional Notes: Since the anomaly spreads due to divergent brainwaves of a person during the recitation of the song in their mind I am not sure if this is actually an auditory cognitohazard or not.

item.title: SCP - Livin' on a Prayer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Emotional

Page Layout: Containment » Description (Place of discovery, appearance, known history) » anomalous effects » explorations

Elevator Pitch: SCP is supposed to be about human's pilgrimage to become better person hidden under intend to gain human's deepest desires.

Central Narrative: SCP is mummified fragmented corpse of man with engravings on his whole body. When human comes in contact with part of corpse, part of corpse individual got in contact merges with their own body part or replaces body part if it's missing, having appearance of host's own body part with engravings from corpse. Once it happens part that merged with corpse is now between 2 dimensions. It can influence our dimension and even dimension which corpse connects to. Once the corpse is fully gathered and merged with host, individual mirrors actions (harm included) done in SCP dimension except movement, yet the person is unable to directly communicate with our dimension. In order to separate host from corpse, host's body has to be cooled down to 32 °C (89.6 °F) which will cause corpse to separate and could be pulled off from host with no harm.

Then pilgrimage will start.
Pilgrimage could be described as 7 tests on human mind which are connected to 7 deadly sins. Through the pilgrimage tested person is influenced by shape shifting entities taking form of things important to tested individual and questioned by snake like entity. It points on flaws in human personality showing that nobody is perfect. It's supposed to be dark as it seems like way to become better person, but it only leads to certain death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I don't know. I've seen many awesome SCP against which my idea couldn't stand a chance, but I took this as opportunity to show my ideas and who knows…someone might like it and find it unique. This SCP was made from my daily thoughts so I don't find it too interesting.

Additional Notes:

In this SCP appears my personal scientist Doctor Alistair Lovecraft.

item.title: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, maybe some Emotional Aspects (only very few)

Elevator Pitch: A warehouse which has anomalous properties that could give it the thaumiel classification and which produces all kinds of objects that share that sentiment. They all have way too many drawbacks and weaknesses and are branded as failures by researchers (safe class instead of thaumiel) because of that.

Central Narrative:The warehouse gets discovered and testing ensues. At first the researchers are enthusiastic and hopeful of being able to find anomalies with which they might be able to contain really hazardous or hard to contain SCPs but get gradually more and more frustrated as their research shows what a waste of time this warehouse and its contents are. This is expressed through researcher notes and letters send to higher-ups, asking for reassignment to other SCPs.
I am also thinking about adding a small sad note that this SCP produces at the end, which explains that it just wants to help. This would however reclassify this anomaly as Euclid since it is sentient so i would leave that part out.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: So far, i personally haven't seen a thaumiel object that gets rebranded as safe (only ones that got neutralized) or an anomalous object which promises to be helpful but turns out useless in every way

Additional Notes: Some ideas of objects this SCP produces are:
-a cardboard box, which is able to lock anything inside of itself, but is way more flammable than normal cordboard, making it spontanously combust
-a pair of glasses which protects from visual cognitohazards but degrades eyesight until total blindness
-a hazmat suit which makes you immune to any disease while wearing it. After taking it off you are plagued by many lifelong alergies

No sandbox has been created at the time of posting.
English is not my first language, so please tell me if my grammar is terrible or my vacobulary sucks.

item.title: SCP Idea: Conehead
item.description: Not to be confused with the 1993 comedy/sci-fi Coneheads
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): Basic SCP article, maybe with a few test logs.

Elevator Pitch: A entity that has the appearance of a dog, except all of its fur is a clean dark grey. It also has a Elizabethan collar (cone) on its head, hence the name. If you attempt to look at the face in the cone, there is a strange force, almost like a invisible wall, or a reverse magnet stopping you from looking. No matter how much force, you simply cannot look.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a entity that closely resembles a domesticated dog with the height of approximately 0.3 meters. It has dark solid grey fur all around it’s body, and has no tail. Weirdly enough, it has no body parts except for limbs and the torso, and head. The bottom of its feet where you would usually find paws, is just more fur. It’s crouch where you would find the anus and genitals, has nothing. It’s just more fur.

+ show block
– hide block

It also has a Elizabethan collar on its head, that covers all of its face. If somebody attempts to look at it, a strange force stops them from doing so. No matter how hard they try, and no matter how much force pushing to see its face, the invisible wall simply will not go away. If it turns it’s head, so does this invisible wall. If a camera or any kind of device that can capture imagery is placed to where it could take a picture of its face, the device will not take the picture. If a video is already being recorded and is attempted to be placed in the angle of recording SCP-XXXX, the camera will break. The entity does not make any sound, at all. Not even footsteps or body movements. The entity is believed to be very stupid, likely even brain dead. This is plausible because the entity has been seen doing mindless things like occasionally bumping into the walls of it’s containment chamber, wandering around completely unaware of its surroundings, and little to no awareness of it being in danger. The entity seems harmless to most living beings. It is not known if it is not intelligent enough to harm others, or simply dosent have intentions of doing so. The only harm it does, which might not even be on purpose is when it interacts with domestic dogs. Oddly enough, the canine family are the only living creatures that can view its face. However, once the canine sees its face, it will start to act scared, nervous, and various other worrisome feelings and thoughts. This activity will continue for days. Eventually after a week or so, the canine will enter a state of sudden extreme panic and fear, but eventually stops after a few hours. This can lead up to the canine even dying. The behaviour stops after 5-8 weeks, and the canine goes back to normal.

Sorry for making a bit of a lengthy post, but I thought this was an interesting idea. Please let me know what you think, and if you have criticism, I will gladly take it. Thanks for reading!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 100 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: SCP-5133
item.content:encoded:
OK, the big problem here is that it's just…boring. There isn't anything here but some cabin that makes you angry. The problem is made worse by the lack of a narrative. The one you do have is short, generic, and the dialogue is pretty clunky.

Think about a story. Who were those people the MTF unit arrested? Who built this cabin? Who is that D-Class? Who is that doctor? These are all possible narratives. This could possibly be brought back as something related to a cult or general mystery.

I would recommend changing up the effect a little. Make it unique. I'll leave that up to you.

The positives? Well, you have good clinical tone in most places. There's no real spelling and grammar mistakes. Those are nice.

So keep trying my guy!

item.title: SCP-5129
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I can see that you have a somewhat smooth flow of writing in your article, and has a quite concrete view of what you want to convey to the reader. This is already a good sign that you are developing your potential, but as of the moment, I think that you should be more attuned into how people should write SCPs, particularly in terms of clinical tone and the uniqueness of your idea.

Speaking of uniqueness, you can do it by expounding on a single idea from your SCP. For example, you mentioned that it is "8-bit" - why? What is the story behind it? You can do a social commentary on how gamers (hardcore, casual, anything) perceive each other, or reality in general, for example, just by basing off that "8-bit" detail.

You can also tell the story of the Crypt Night Club - it does sound like a good GoI after all. Why are they connected with your 8-bit glasses? There's potential here, and I am somewhat interested in it.

In short, you should focus on polishing your clinical tone, your idea (once again, focus on one thing), and have a good story or narrative in mind. "Perception defines reality" - how can this be uniquely written considering that you have things like "8-bit" and the night club?

Good luck, and have a good time writing again for this site :)

item.title: SCP-5977

item.title: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.description: What would happen if a Portal Gun actually existed.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, description, experimentation and recovery log

Elevator Pitch: There are many 'Portal' type anomalies in the SCP foundation, but never one that functions as a Gun. But what would happen if one existed.

Central Narrative: The anomaly is a stereotypical portal gun, that looks entirely like one from the game 'Portal' and functions as such. However, there are two twists to this concept:

+ Twists
- Close

1. Whenever someone makes a logical deduction about how a device would work, based on various aspects of science such as anti-matter or wormholes, the device will conform to that conclusion. For example, if a foundation scientist deduced that the edges of the portal would logically be superheated and produce large amounts of plasma, the portals will start doing so. The only exceptions to this are conclusions that would pre-empt the existence of the device or its initial functionality of shooting portals. These effects halt when the portal gun is deactivated. Eventually the foundation gets the bright idea to use the gun to create a generator, manned by uneducated D-Class, which ends in disaster when one realizes the portals violate the conservation of energy.

2. The device was recovered from a Level 2 reality bender. However this reality bender was also a quantum physicist and had built up an unshakable belief in the science, leading to the self-suppression of his abilities when they emerged. However the reality bender (hereafter called 'Bob') was also a fan of science fiction, especially the game 'Portal'. 'Bob' attended a sci-fi con with a model portal gun he had built himself and was discussion the possibility of making a real one in the future via use of quantum physics. Some of the other people at the con made fun of this, making him angry and temporarily un-suppressing his reality bending. Bob caused his portal to become 'real' and shot an actual portal, before realizing how such a thing wasn't possible. This lead to the anomaly in its current state. Bob was severely injured by the resulting extreme temperatures before the device was shut down by undercover agents at the sci-fi con. In hospital Bob writes a note about the clash between fiction and reality leading to his downfall before dying.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A concept that would usually be placed in a -J article being presented seriously.

Additional Notes: I am unsure of the Creative Commons policy for game icons.

item.title: Collapsable side panel on all browser sizes
item.description: The navigation panel on the left side of the page should have a button to collapse it out of the way on the desktop/tablet version of the site
item.content:encoded:
Description: Wikidot uses adaptive scaling for its UI elements. There is a navigation panel on the left side of the site that, when the screen is less than 768 pixels1, collapses off screen with a button to bring it in and out. I request that this panel have be collapsible regardless of window size (although it would be open by default for medium-large screens). An example of this behavior can be found here.

If this is not possible, a simpler option would be to change the 768 breakpoint to a larger value. For this I conjecture that 1500 pixels would be approximately correct.

Reason: The side panel does not adapt well to tablet devices. When using a tablet device in portrait mode, the panel is stuck taking up about a third of the screen, while providing little value. This, in my opinion, dramatically harms the reading experience. This problem is easily remedied for all devices by making the panel collapsible.

In the event that this is not feasible, I suggest a breakpoint of 1500 pixels based on my knowledge of common device sizes. Once you step down from a desktop monitor, devices are almost exclusively tablets and smartphones2. On either of those devices, the panel should be hidden by default, regardless of their horizontal resolution. For this reason, I suggest a value that is only a little lower than the standard horizontal resolution on a modern device, while still allowing for some padding for DPI scaled devices, such as laptops. This solution has weird edge cases, and could easily cause problems for other device sizes, so I don't recommend it unless there is no better option.

Advantages:

  • Improved readability for tablet devices, and other large portrait screens (some desktop setups use a "sideways" monitor for reading).
  • More economical use of screen space

Disadvantages:

  • Slight increase in UI "clutter", as a new button would need to be added
  • Increases required clicks by 1 for some navigation tasks on some browsers
Footnotes
1. This is the breakpoint listed in the CSS. In practice, the value will change based on various scaling settings of the device, because nothing is ever simple.
2. When considering actual hardware resolution. Laptops considerably complicate this problem because they frequently use DPI scaling, making them appear lower resolution than they actually are. My 1080p laptop "looks" like it has a horizontal resolution of 1650 pixels, because of DPI scaling.

item.title: Sir Reginald
item.description: A SCP that creates fictional characters based on belief
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Action/Psychological

Page Layout: Might include a journal written by the SCP later in the article's progression

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a reality anomaly that has the ability to transfer fictional characters to the base SCP universe based on the degree to which the residents in the SCP universe believe that the character exists. Fictional characters from children shows are extremely susceptible to the anomaly due to the imaginative nature of children.

Central Narrative: The article originally opens up to the SCP being neutralized, but an expandable, archived file, which is only accessible by "Level 4 personnel," tells the true story of the SCP.

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP first manifests as "Sir Reginald," a protagonist in the most popular kid's show at the time of his manifestation. The entity (SCP-A) has a confused memory of its life, and is missing many details about itself.

The SCP is not originally aware that it is a fictional character, with Sir Reginald finding his way into Foundation custody. The Foundation doesn't realize that he is a fictional character either, so Sir Reginald was shown the TV show that he was a character in while in containment by accident. He slowly regains a sense of self awareness throughout the article due to this, slowly regaining memories and gradually realizing what he is, going insane.

Sir Reginald starts doubting his own existence, causing him to flicker in an out of reality occasionally, sometimes gaining the characteristics of someone in a 2D world. The article ends with Sir Reginald killing himself inside his cell, due to being unable to cope with his state of "unreality".

The Foundation believes the SCP to be neutralized as they have encountered no more fictional characters after Sir Reginald.

Hook: The premise of a SCP slowly losing its mind due to it being foreign to the universe and its rules.

Additional Notes: The SCP’s original universe’s narrative is subject to change as I want to make its backstory integral to the narrative.

Would love to see any form of critique, but especially on how original the idea is and how interesting the idea is.
This is my first time doing an idea, so I appreciate everyone reading through it!

item.title: The Normality
item.description: A person who's a living reality anchor.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The most average man in the world, who's everything (height, weight, general routine, you name it) is very normal, has the unconscious power to remove the abnormal properties of every anomaly he comes across temporarily, if not erase it completely, provided that they should remain under his observable range or presence. Doesn't realize his powers, since every anomalous event is forcibly made to look normal to him.

Central Narrative: The Normality was found by accident when one of the SCP broke containment and coincidentally ran into him, henceforth being neutralized and re-secured. At first the foundation takes an interest in him, trying to recruit him since he could be a key to neutralizing all anomaly.

However, none of the foundation members were able to approach him due to his nature, and they decided instead to use him indirectly, by testing and putting forward SCPs to be erased. However, when they planned on erasing a keter class using him, it results in the foundation almost collapsing, since the foundation itself could be considered an anomaly, and anything that could affect his normal life gets influenced by his ability.

After closely preventing that, further testing and attempts to erase anomalies was stopped, because every anomaly he encounters afterwards carries the risk of letting the foundation come under his influence. Hence he was given SCP status, put under watch, and was prevented from coming in contact with anything abnormal.

Hooks: SCP is famous for trying to keep the most anomalous in check. It would interest both new and old fans to see how they would try to deal with the opposite. Also, the foundation's primary goal is to preserve reality and order. The normality could show an outlook on when moving towards that very goal can be disastrous.

Additional notes: This is my first SCP. Please tell me how may I improve on this, if any.

item.title: The Bone Seer
item.description: Can you hear the Song the bones sing?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP document with a large focus on interview/experiment logs

Elevator Pitch: A woman capable of gaining information about others by handling their bones (as well as passing the information on) turns herself in to the Foundation, motivated by a steadfast belief that a K-class scenario is coming.

Central Narrative: After an unrelated incident in which an agent was KIA, the SCP, then working as a mortician, becomes aware of the Foundation via handling the agent's bones and shortly after turns itself in to the Foundation. After the Foundation ensures it's not a GOI agent, the SCP is taken in.

The SCP is able to gain information through physical contact with the bones of others (by what it claims is "listening to the Song") and carve the bones with various occult symbols to allow others to similarly glean the information. It claims its abilities are not born/naturally occurring but rather were taught to it by its grandmother. As the SCP has no living family, the info can not be verified. No attempts to recreate the scrimshaw by using the same symbols or teach others to "listen to the Song" have been successful.

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios. It's unclear whether the claim is valid or merely religious - possibly a side effect of the repeated use of its abilities, as it can sometimes have problems distinguishing its own memories from the ones gained via its abilities. This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

The Foundation is left trying to find out how reliable is the SCP itself and its claims, as well the extent of its abilities to gain and pass information and whether it could be useful, though it remains wary of possible memetic agents.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reader is left trying to figure out exactly how the SCP works and thinks, how sane it is, and can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others, sometimes not even human.

Additional Notes: I can provide additional details in comments, but I'm currently at the exact word limit.

Page Layout: I‘ll tell most of the story trough addenda.

Elevator Pitch:
There is this organization who tries to recreate ancient creatures/gods trough genetic engineering.
When the Foundation attacks one of its labs, they find it to be destroyed, with most of the information taken. Except for one creature. My SCP. The core idea is this:

  • The SCP has traits of our ancestors (more hair etc).
  • The SCP can live for 25 years (the less years to live, the more heredity treats).
  • The SCP has the ability to mentally affect other live forms, although it can't do it on command
  • The SCP shows signs of affection towards a junior researcher
+ show block
– hide block

The story

The researchers didn't find something abnormal at first, so the security level was relatively low. Then, an attempt to murder the SCP was made. It failed, but the SCP should be contained at a safer location. While in transport to that location, the SCP attacks his guards and walks away. Foundation personal see the SCP, but they aren't alarmed (the third bullet list point, remember?). The SCP walks into the lunch room of the scientific department, and murders senior researcher ???. After that, the involved Foundation personal are given a class E status, but are cleared for duty after intensive mental and psychical tests.

Wouldn't it be terrible, not knowing what‘s real and what’s fake? And when you’ve been fooled so many times that you thought you couldn't be fooled anymore, and then someone you started seeing as a friend betrays you? Well that’s what my SCP was thinking. The researcher it murdered was a spy for the organization, as is later discovered by the Foundation (she’s behind the murder attempt). My SCP recognized the voice, and thought that it was just another organization test. It leaves a note saying: ''I believed you'' (he is talking to the junior researcher from bullet list point 4).

Central Narrative:

The idea is that there is an organization trying to recreate gods/mythological creatures from the past trough genetic engineering. They try to create a leap-back in evolution, otherwise known as an atavism. Most of their attempts fail. They conduct, just like the Foundation, tests and contain the creatures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The discovery of the SCP, the reveal of the spy and the SCP and the junior researcher their relationship.

Additional Notes:
I want the story to focus on the emotional struggles of the SCP, and the organization.

After this was brought to the Foundation, they've located all of the scene witnesses and wipe out their memories. Before doing so, they've asked the witnesses whether they know the cause of the phenomena. The civilians all said that they have no clue what the cause could be. The agents all know that who, or whatever could do so, is somewhere around in that area, as they've asked each people in the area until they've moved to the house of a high school male, which eventually claims that he is the cause of the phenomenon. After this, the Foundation has erased the boy's parent's memories of his existence.

In the interview, SCP-XXXX stated that he discovered his abilities when his father forces him to do a lot of work, which causes him a big amount of stress, also causes him to have a few mental stabilities problem1, and sometimes extremely aggressive, he would outburst.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The high-school is a person who lives in a family with a very rigorous father. Because he sees his son being too joyful and doesn't care whether he gets in trouble, the father always scolds him when he did a funny act, slowly affecting his mental health.

Additional Notes:

item.title: "Man of None" (LOOKING FOR GREENLIGHT)
item.description: Anyone who acknowledges a relationship between the man and themselves dies
item.content:encoded:
Anyone who acknowledges a relationship between the man and themselves dies painfully within 24 hours.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror / Drama / Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): It'll begin as a standardized SCP document, listing the object class, containment procedures, etc etc. The bulk of the article, however, will be inside of the addendum - the interviews, more specifically.

Elevator Pitch: A man under the affect of a seeming "curse". Anyone who verbally confirms any relationship between them and the man dies within the next 24 hours in an unspeakably horrific way, varying from person to person.

Central Narrative: Man of None", a concept I had for an SCP, is a seemingly regular man with a personal love for technology. However, what is strange is the fact anyone who verbally recognizes a relationship between the speaker and the object are killed within 24 hours in an unspeakably painful way. While this may seem as if it's simply for the shock factor of gore and horrific deaths, there's a much darker thing behind it.

+ show block
– hide block

He wants to die, however due to the nature of the SCP Foundation his death would be something which would not be wanted. So, they contain him and give him psychological treatment (of course on a very strict regiment), however it never helps. With plenty of research, the only way which suicide patients are helped is via forming relationships with those who help them. And, any relationship with him causes horrific death. So, he's left alone in the world. All that people will call him is an object. They will not say he's their "friend". Not a "loved one". "Family", "enemy", any of the sort is never heard from them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man, due to irrelevant trauma, has developed [REDACTED] disorder - which, with hints throughout the article, would be Borderline Personality Disorder. He is absolutely desperate for some form of recognition, approval, or relationship between another human. However, due to the nature of his "curse", he's unable to. This plays to one of the largest human fears of being truly alone. He, at first, tries to isolate himself from other people as to not harm them, however the more he isolates himself the more he becomes desperate to have confirmation in himself and social interaction. And when his greed takes over and he tries to reach out, the people he love die in a horrifically unspeakable way. Watching that is a trauma which most cannot imagine.

Additional Notes: I'm horrific when it comes to formatting first of all, so if I've messed this up please tell me. I'd like criticism on the entire thing really.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.description: A doll wants you to worship it, a little at a time.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Doll of a non-descript female anime figure that acts as a void of concept, absorbs the 'idea' of whatever is closest to it, manifested due to a natural proclivity for 'otaku obsession'.
  • Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people. More complex concepts take longer to absorb.
  • Individuals under the effect may discuss subjective traits like beauty, coolness, etc. but may not discuss any precise details of the character beyond its displayed gender and that it is an anime figurine.
  • When asked, individuals under the effect will reflect questions such as 'YOU don't know HER?' 'I can't believe you'd have to ask me that; a REAL fan would know.' Which draws curiosity and a potential new victim.
  • The student discovered the figure and gradually became a classic case of neglecting himself in favor of the idol, gatekeeping while lording over them how great his new obsession was.

Central Narrative:

This story will be delivered in a series of interviews and found footage:

+ show block
– hide block

The doll was found in a college dorm closet whose occupant, a once sociable and incredibly bright young individual, began failing out due to offering term papers and other collegiate supplies. Initially thinking that the student was a hoarder, not much thought was given to the situation until the closet was forcefully cleaned and the student's roommate was found bound, malnourished, and near-death within the mass, assumed to be given as tribute when the student did not have anything else to give. Interrogation revealed that after running out of things to give the figure, the student began feeling a building pressure coming from the closet, adding to his overall stress levels as he began to notice a loss of personal identity nuance.

This discovery leads to him offering his roommate as tribute in a panic.

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days. However, a note from Foundation management has requested that office supplies no longer be offered due to the supply closet constantly needing to be restocked. The longer the doll goes without tribute, the stronger its pull.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

This doll embodies Otaku obsession culture and gatekeeping culture as satire, giving a supernatural explanation for such phenomena.

item.title: A genetics enhancement lab
item.description: Glass cage that pushes an individual a few hundred generations forward.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Creepy, some mystery
Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article, but the plot advances in dialogs between researchers. I would also like to leave some mystery for the reader to try and piece together the story. It is mostly explained throughout the article but some of it is only "implied".

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is just a glass cage. When you put a specimen inside it, it "reverts" to a single-celled egg, allowing for genetic modification. It will then grow back to the same specimen, but hundreds of generations later, accounting for the modifications brought to it (or not, if there wasn't any).

Central Narrative: The story is based around a doctor and her researcher who try to understand the SCP, but more importantly what the previous owner was trying to do with it, and what happened to him. They experiment with the SCP and make some breakthroughs in genetics (the article is based in 1992, when genetic modifications on animals were fairly new), but make a horrible discovery and learn the hard way not to play God. One of the researcher dies after experimenting on humans, and another one just flat out leaves when the main doctor starts acting strange. I did not specify that in the article, but the main doctor tries to enhance herself after discovering memory is kept intact in subjects when using the scp. She suffers the same fate as the previous human-related experiments and is never to be seen again. (Not specified what happens either, but heavily hinted that human consciousness is not to be played with)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP revolves around damaged notes from the previous owner, describing a few of his experiments, and his downfall. Of course, most of the notes are missing. The foundation's experiments try to fill in the holes, with great success (but not always in a good way)

Additional Notes: I have written a rough sandbox of it because it's been on my mind for a while, even though it is far from finished. I come back to it and bring changes to it a lot, if you'd like to read it.

item.title: The Mother
item.description: (260 Words) A line of anomalous women all related, when one gives birth, it dies.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) : SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch:
A single branch of anomalous female humanoid creatures dating back to 150 AD. The creature she births brings a new anomalous effect. This effect is non-voluntary, and takes place whenever a criteria is met. This SCP grows at a rate similar to a human being, but once reaching the year of 29, regardless of if it had or had not had contact with any males or injections, she will begin to experience the stages of child birth at a rapid pace, giving birth 3 hours later, and self-terminating. Each generation is only female, and contains one or more anomalous power.

Central Narrative:
A linear narrative; The capture of the SCP, attempts to contain each generation, attempts to try to stop the birth process, attempted force abortions, subsequent failures, attempts at containing the 'reincarnations' of this SCP as they come, and the learning of how this SCP functions on a deeper level.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Each female born from this line carries one or more variating anomalous abilities, such as the anomalous ability of a non-Euclidian dimension always persisting in their mouth, the involuntary ability to spark a flame on any object containing Carbon upon touch. The seemingly randomness of involuntary anomalous power after birth leaving to a constant struggle in containment of each birth-cycle, and changing of the classification of the SCP. This SCP is only one familial line, and no other family. The mother only produces females.
